newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS AND TWO RELIEVERS THREE-HIT WHITE SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS AND TWO RELIEVERS THREE-HIT WHITE SOX.

text.p: Roger Clemens pitched 5-2/3 scoreless innings before leaving with an injury and Joe Carter and Ed Sprague drove in two runs each as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Chicago White Sox 5-0 on a three hitter on Wednesday.
The temperature was just above freezing and just 746 people attended the game.
"Everybody in the major leagues has played in cold weather," White Sox manager Terry Bevington said. "It's something that can be expected at this time of year. But it's the same for both teams."

Clemens, a three-time Cy Young Award winner, left with a muscle cramp in his right groin after fanning Tony Phillips and Dave Martinez to open the sixth. He didn't allow a hit after the second inning and retired 12 of the last 13 batters he faced.
In Anaheim, Mark Whiten went 4-for-4 and Mariano Duncan had three hits and three RBI to lead an 18-hit attack as the New York Yankees rolled to a 12-5 victory over the Anaheim Angels.
David Wells (1-0) pitched a nine-hitter, allowing five earned runs with two walks and three strikeouts as the Yankees split their season-opening eight-game West Coast road trip.
The Angels' Allen Watson was ripped for eight runs and 10 hits in 2-1/3 innings.

In Detroit, pinch-hitter Jody Reed and Bubba Trammell had RBI singles in the seventh inning and Bobby Higginson blasted a grand slam in the eighth as the Detroit Tigers posted a 10-5 victory over the Minnesota Twins.

John Cummings picked up the win after entering the game with men on first and second and one out in the seventh. He caught Paul Molitor attempting to steal third and then induced Matt Lawton to ground out to first to end the threat.

In Kansas City, Jeffrey Hammonds stroked a two-run double in the top of the 11th inning and five relievers combined to pitch five scoreless innings as the Baltimore Orioles defeated the Kansas City Royals, 4-2 in a game played in a steady snowfall.
"I wanted to stay aggressive every swing," Hammonds said. "I was going to try to get that run in. I faced him (Bevil) in Puerto Rico before. I knew he wss going to throw the hard slider."
Jay Bell hit a two-run homer in the sixth for Kansas City. which is 1-3 against Baltimore this season.
In Oakland, Scott Brosius drew a bases-loaded walk off Rick Trlicek with two out in the bottom of the 10th inning to give the Oakland Athletics a 4-3 victory over the Boston Red Sox.
Aaron Small (1-0), who arrived at the Oakland Coliseum during the game after he was recalled from Triple-A Edmonton, pitched a perfect 10th to get the win.
"I got up (in Colorado Springs) at 4:28 this morning. (There was) snow on the ground," Small said. "It was a fun day. I'm still going on the peanuts and crackers I ate on the plane."
In Seattle, Joey Cora's two-run single capped a six-run first inning and Bob Wolcott pitched 6-2/3 scoreless innings as the Seattle Mariners routed the Cleveland Indians 11-1.
"I would have liked to finish the seventh inning but it's early in the season and there's no point in wearing myself out in a game where we're up 11-0," Wolcott said."
